new_findings_today.title: refresh-stay-picks-agent's network egress block is now an 8th-plus consecutive occurrence spanning over a week, with repeated 'FOUNDER ACTION NEEDED' self-reports that have never been actioned
new_findings_today.detail: Direct read of the refresh-stay-picks-agent job's own latest ops_reports run record (2026-08-18T22:24:21 UTC, batch of 20 destinations incl. ponda-spice) shows its verification_note explicitly stating: 'This is the same unresolved block this job has now logged on at least 2026-08-10, 08-11, 08-12, 08-13, 08-14, 08-15, and 08-17 -- at least the 8th consecutive occurrence spanning 9 calendar days, with FOUNDER ACTION NEEDED raised on every one of those runs and never actioned.' The underlying issue: scripts/verify-touched-pages.mjs gets a 403 on the HTTPS CONNECT tunnel to www.nakshiq.com from that job's own scheduled-session network-policy sandbox (confirmed via 3 independent methods in its own run: direct curl, the HTTPS_PROXY agentproxy status endpoint, and WebFetch's EGRESS_BLOCKED error) -- this is a policy denial specific to THAT job's sandbox, not a site outage (this QA session's own sandbox reached nakshiq.com without any issue for the entire A-L probe + Chrome E2E pass). The job has a documented substitute-verification method (DB constraint + component null-safety checks) that gives reasonable confidence the written data is structurally sound, and the canary-probe cron remains an independent live safety net, so this is not evidence of a live site defect. It is flagged here because prior daily QA passes have only carried this as a passing 'needs_review, carried not new' note inside ops_reports_targeted_check_note, which has let an explicitly self-escalating, repeatedly-unactioned blocker stay quiet for over a week.
